technical.lead: Databricks open-sources Omnigent, a meta-harness wrapping Claude Code, Codex and agent SDKs
technical.body: Databricks introduced Omnigent on June 13, an Apache 2.0 (alpha) open-source meta-harness that sits one layer above individual coding agents and agent SDKs so a developer drives several through one interface. It wraps command-line agents (Claude Code, Codex, Pi) and SDKs (OpenAI Agents, Claude Agents SDK) so implementations swap without rewriting, enforces stateful, contextual policy at the meta-harness layer (cost budgets, permissions, OS-level sandboxing), and exposes live agent sessions shareable by URL for teammates to review files, comment and steer the same run. Sessions span web, mobile, a macOS app and APIs, with cloud execution on Modal and Daytona sandboxes and multi-harness agents authored in YAML. It shipped as a standalone GitHub project (omnigent-ai/omnigent) alongside the Data + AI Summit rather than a Databricks-only feature.

technical.lead: CacheRL trains small tool-calling agents near frontier accuracy with cached rollouts at ~100x less compute
technical.body: A June 12 arXiv paper, CacheRL: Multi-Turn Tool-Calling Agents via Cached Rollouts and Hybrid Reward (arXiv:2606.14179), targets the most expensive part of fine-tuning small agent models: reinforcement learning over multi-turn tool use normally requires live tool execution thousands of times per batch. CacheRL replays a three-tier fuzzy cache of past trajectories with token-level masking to avoid live calls, and pairs it with a cache-tier-aware hybrid reward that reweights answer quality so the model is not penalized for limitations the cache introduces. The authors report 92% process accuracy on multi-step tool-calling, approaching GPT-5's reported 94%, while using roughly 100x less compute, and lift validation reward on Qwen3-4B-Thinking from 0.43 to 0.78; ablations credit a 41% drop to removing knowledge transfer and a 17% gain to the cache-aware reward. The result is a concrete recipe for distilling tool-calling competence into a small open model without a costly live-execution RL loop.

technical.lead: Databricks Data + AI Summit opens Monday, anchoring a three-track summer AI calendar
technical.body: The Databricks Data + AI Summit opens today and runs June 15-18 across Moscone in San Francisco (30,000-plus in person from 150-plus countries; keynotes from co-founders Ali Ghodsi, Matei Zaharia, Arsalan Tavakoli-Shiraji and Reynold Xin, plus OpenAI's Greg Brockman, a recorded Satya Nadella fireside and a multi-day hackathon with OpenAI), anchoring a summer calendar across three tracks. Dev/data continues with the AI Engineer World's Fair June 29-July 2 at Moscone West (dedicated Inference and Security tracks). AI-security spans the Confidential Computing Summit June 23-24 at the San Francisco Mint, SecurityWeek's AI Risk Summit August 11-12, Black Hat USA's AI Summit inside the August 1-6 conference, and OWASP Global AppSec USA November 5-6. AI-chip/hardware spans AMD's Advancing AI 2026 on July 23 at Moscone (Instinct/MI400-series focus expected), Hot Chips 2026 at Stanford August 23-25, and the AI Infra Summit September 15-17 in Santa Clara.

technical.lead: Omnigent looks set to become a paid Databricks-managed agent-orchestration tier by Q2 2027
technical.body: Omnigent shipped as a standalone Apache 2.0 OSS project (omnigent-ai/omnigent) alongside the Data + AI Summit rather than a Databricks-only feature, which reads as the opening move of an open-core go-to-market rather than a charity release - the same playbook that built Databricks around open-source Spark and Delta. Giving away the orchestration and policy layer seeds adoption and makes Omnigent the default control point a team standardizes on, while the durable revenue is the managed runtime, hosted execution, identity and governance underneath. The forward thesis: by Q2 2027 Databricks publicly offers a priced, Databricks-hosted Omnigent-based product - a managed runtime, hosted/cloud execution, or enterprise governance tier that is generally available or in paid preview, tied to Databricks-billed consumption (DBUs) or a subscription. The counter-risk is that Databricks keeps Omnigent purely community OSS and monetizes agents only through its existing Mosaic AI / Agent Bricks surface.

technical.lead: Meta-harness emerges as the cross-vendor policy plane for enterprise agents by H1 2027
technical.body: The structurally significant part of Omnigent is not its unified driver surface but where the guardrails live: it enforces stateful, contextual policy at the meta-harness layer itself, tracking each wrapped agent's actions and applying cost budgets, permissions and OS-level sandboxing across whichever runtime is underneath. That relocates the natural control point for enterprise agent governance upward, from per-runtime configuration scattered across each vendor's own harness to a single vendor-neutral layer that brokers, observes and constrains them all. The prediction: by H1 2027 at least one more independent vendor or hyperscaler ships an agent meta-harness whose headline capability is enforcing policy (budgets, permissions, sandboxing or audit) uniformly across two or more rival agent runtimes, or an enterprise-agent governance framework names the meta-harness layer as the prescribed policy-enforcement point. A single-vendor harness that only governs its own agents, or routing with no cross-runtime guardrail enforcement, would not count.
